newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to hit deficit goal, do all needed - Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: France to hit deficit goal, do all needed - Arthuis.

text.p: Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday the French government was set on strictly respecting its targets of reducing the public deficit to three percent of GDP in 1997 and 2.8 percent in 1998.
He said in a statement issued by the finance ministry that evidence so far this year showed no sign of a slippage.
"In any case, the government will take sufficient steps to respect its target for the public deficit of three percent of GDP in 1997, if necessary," the statement said.

Arthuis reiterated that the government was forecasting GDP growth of at least 2.3 percent this year and that the budget deficit to the end of February was 17.6 billion francs less than at the same stage in 1996.

The ministry response came amid increasing media questions about the need for further spending cut measures to ensure that the government respected the deficit target this year -- the test year for qualifying for European monetary union.
Arthuis reiterated that the government had already decided to freeze 10 billion francs or spending credits in addition to the spending cuts in the initial 1997 budget.
The French budget deficit, reported by the Finance Ministry on Tuesday, stood at 72.4 billion francs at the end of February, versus 90 billion francs at the same stage in 1996.
